stem:
Mei Ling set up a circuit with two bulbs, a buzzer and two switches. The table shows what she observed.

| Switch 1 | Switch 2 | Number of bulbs lit | Buzzer sounds? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Closed | Closed | 2 | Yes |
| Closed | Open | 1 | No |
| Open | Closed | 1 | Yes |

Which circuit matches her observations?
options: Bulb A in series with switch 1; bulb B and buzzer in series with switch 2, on a parallel branch
Bulb A and buzzer in series with switch 1 on one branch; bulb B alone on a second branch, switch 2 in the main loop
Both bulbs in series with switch 1; buzzer alone with switch 2 on a parallel branch
All components in one series loop with both switches
working: When S1 only is closed, 1 bulb lights and no buzzer → bulb A must be on a branch with S1 alone. When S2 only is closed, 1 bulb + buzzer → bulb B and buzzer share the S2 branch. Both closed → 2 bulbs + buzzer. Only (1) gives all three rows.
Watch out: Option (2): with S2 in the main loop, opening S2 would switch everything off, contradicting row 2.

stem:
Study the circuit below. All bulbs and batteries are working.

Which statement is correct?
options: Bulb P is brighter than bulb Q.
Bulbs Q and R are brighter than bulb P.
If bulb Q fuses, bulb P will not light up.
If bulb P fuses, bulbs Q and R will not light up.
working: P is alone on its branch; Q and R share a branch in series so each gets less current and is dimmer. Branches are independent, so one fusing does not affect the other branch.
Watch out: Students think 'more bulbs on a branch = more light'. In series, more bulbs = dimmer.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Ravi put equal numbers of two kinds of fish into each of two identical tanks with the same amount of water plants. Tank X had fish J and K. Tank Y had fish J and L. The graphs show his results over a week.

Which food chain shows the relationship among the organisms?
options: Plant → J → K → L
Plant → K → J → L
Plant → K → L → J
Plant → L → K → J
working: Tank X: K fell while J rose → J eats K. Tank Y: J fell while L rose → L eats J. K is eaten and eats no fish, so K eats the plants: Plant → K → J → L.
Watch out: Reading the falling line as the predator. The population that DROPS is the prey.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Jody filled a beaker completely with ice cubes and left it in a room at 25 °C. The graph shows the temperature of the contents over 25 minutes.

He made two changes to the set-up at the 10th and 20th minute. Which changes did he make?
options: 10th: added ice cubes; 20th: added tap water
10th: added a heat source; 20th: added ice cubes
10th: added a heat source; 20th: added a heat source
10th: added ice cubes; 20th: removed the heat source
working: 0–4 min: flat at 0 °C while the ice melts. Then the water warms to 25 °C, the room temperature, and stays there: without heat it can't get warmer than the room. From 10 min it climbs steeply to 100 °C → a heat source was added. At 20 min it drops sharply → something cold was added (ice), and it then rises again because the heat source is still on. Removing the heat source would give a slow fall, not a sharp drop.
Watch out: The flat parts at 0 °C and 100 °C are melting and boiling: temperature stays the same during a change of state.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Three identical springs, X, Y and Z, were hung from a ceiling with loads of different masses. The diagram shows the stretched lengths.

Which statement is correct?
options: Load P has the greatest mass.
Spring Z exerts the greatest elastic spring force.
The three loads have the same mass.
Spring X is stretched the most.
working: Identical springs stretch more when pulled by a heavier load. Z stretched most → R is heaviest → Z exerts the greatest elastic spring force (it must hold up the heaviest load).
Watch out: Confusing the spring's length with its 'elasticity'. Identical springs have the same elasticity; the difference is the load.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Jun Hao placed an aquatic plant in a test tube of water and shone a lamp on it in a dark room. He counted the bubbles produced in one minute, then moved the lamp further away and repeated.

| | Changed variable | Measured variable | Kept the same |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (1) | Number of bubbles per minute | Distance of lamp | Type of plant |
| (2) | Distance of lamp | Number of bubbles per minute | Type of plant |
| (3) | Type of lamp | Distance of lamp | Number of bubbles |
| (4) | Distance of lamp | Size of bubbles | Type of test tube |

Which row correctly identifies the variables?
options: Row (1)
Row (2)
Row (3)
Row (4)
working: He CHANGED the lamp distance on purpose; he MEASURED the bubbles per minute (the result); the plant, water and lamp stay the same for a fair test.
Watch out: Swapping changed and measured variables. Ask: 'What did he do on purpose?' (changed) vs 'What did he count/record?' (measured).

stem:
The diagram shows a cross-section of a flower.

| | Part | Name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | J | Stigma | Receives pollen grains |
| B | K | Anther | Produces pollen grains |
| C | L | Ovary | Produces pollen grains |
| D | M | Filament | Holds up the anther |

Which row correctly matches the part, its name and its function?
options: A and B only
A, B and D only
B and C only
C and D only
working: Stigma receives pollen (A ✓). Anther makes pollen = male reproductive cells (B ✓). Ovary contains ovules, the FEMALE cells — not pollen (C ✗). Filament holds up the anther (D ✓).
Watch out: Ovary vs anther: ovary → ovules (female); anther → pollen (male). 'Ov' = female (egg).
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
The diagram shows the life cycle of insect X.

Which statements describe insect X correctly?
A: Its young looks like the adult.   B: The missing stage is the pupa.   C: Its young does not have wings.   D: It has three stages in its life cycle.
options: A and B only
B and C only
A and D only
C and D only
working: Egg → larva → ? → adult is the 4-stage cycle (butterfly, beetle, mosquito, housefly). The missing stage is the pupa. The larva looks nothing like the adult and has no wings.
Watch out: 3-stage insects (cockroach, grasshopper, dragonfly) have a NYMPH that looks like a small wingless adult. 4-stage insects have a larva + pupa.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Siti poured 300 ml of hot water at 80 °C into two identical cups, A and B. She wrapped cup B with a thick layer of cotton wool. She measured the temperature of the water in each cup every 5 minutes.

(a) Predict which cup of water will be at a lower temperature after 20 minutes. Explain your answer.
answer: Cup A. Cotton wool traps air, and air is a poor conductor of heat, so heat from the water in cup B is lost to the cooler surroundings more slowly. Water in A loses heat faster and reaches a lower temperature.
marking: 1 mark for choosing A; 1 mark for 'cotton wool / trapped air is a poor conductor of heat so heat is lost more slowly'. Must say HEAT is LOST (not 'cold gets in').
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
Siti poured 300 ml of hot water at 80 °C into two identical cups, A and B. She wrapped cup B with a thick layer of cotton wool. She measured the temperature of the water in each cup every 5 minutes.

(b) Siti repeated the experiment using ice-cold water at 5 °C instead of hot water. Which cup would reach room temperature first? Explain.
answer: Cup A. Heat from the warmer surroundings is gained by the cold water. The cotton wool around cup B slows down the gain of heat, so cup A gains heat faster and reaches room temperature first.
marking: Choice (1) + reason must mention heat GAINED from surroundings and cotton wool slowing heat gain (1). Same idea as (a) in reverse — insulators slow heat flow in BOTH directions.
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
The diagram shows a food web in a garden.

(a) Name one organism that is both a prey and a predator.
answer: Bird or lizard (they eat grasshoppers and are eaten by the hawk).
notes: Figure rendered from figure_spec on 27 Oct by scripts/render-figures.ts; founder to check it.

stem:
The diagram shows a food web in a garden.

(b) A farmer sprayed insecticide that killed most of the grasshoppers. Explain how this would affect the population of caterpillars after a few weeks.
answer: The caterpillar population would decrease. With fewer grasshoppers, the birds and lizards have less food, so they feed more on caterpillars.
marking: 1 mark: decrease. 1 mark: birds/lizards switch to eating more caterpillars because their other food (grasshopper) is gone. NOT 'more grass for caterpillars so they increase' — the predator effect comes first.
